clue.text: Mechanic about to return on locomotive

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so the short word is read from right to left

blocks.note: a locomotive is a railway engine
RE is Latin-derived shorthand for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A railway mechanic is about to climb back onto the locomotive he works on.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed RE sits after the engine: 'on' just joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An engineer is a person who maintains or repairs machinery, which is what a mechanic does.

clue.text: Another bit player

blocks.note: first meaning: one more, additional
second meaning: a film actor with a tiny non-speaking part

explanation.walkthrough: 'Another bit player' reads as one more small actor; split it after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, and an extra is also a background performer in a film crowd scene.

clue.text: Statesman, happy one seen crossing street

indicators.note: a figure seen crossing a road straddles it, so the abbreviation is enclosed by the other pieces

blocks.note: glad means happy
taken as written
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A cheerful politician is spotted walking across a road.
explanation.walkthrough: The street is not crossed by the happy one alone: the words 'happy one' are read together as the outer pair that encloses it.
explanation.definitionFit: William Gladstone was a Victorian statesman who served four times as British prime minister.

clue.text: Just beginning climb after noon

indicators.note: one thing coming after another follows it, so the climb is placed second

blocks.note: N is short for noon
a climb is an ascent

explanation.surface: A hike is only just getting under way after midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means coming into existence, so something nascent is only just beginning.

clue.text: This should get you there quicker from state school

definitions.text: This should get you there quicker

blocks.note: to state something is to express it
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Advice that a state school offers a faster route to success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State school' reads as a single noun, but each word is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: An express train makes few stops, so it reaches its destination faster than a stopping service.

clue.text: Outcome of increased exposure

blocks.note: prices that have increased are up
an exposure on a film is a photographic shot

explanation.surface: Someone notes the result of giving something more publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exposure' reads as publicity, but here it is a single frame of photographic film.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot of a matter is its final result or conclusion, a synonym for outcome.

clue.text: Hebridean isle almost rounded by fellow explorer

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the island's name loses its last letter
being rounded by something means being surrounded, so the island goes inside the other word

blocks.note: a peer is a fellow, an equal
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: A fellow explorer has nearly sailed right round a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is one of the first to explore or settle new territory, so an explorer.

clue.text: Monster in Hardy novel

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A monster appears in a novel by Thomas Hardy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book by Hardy; it is an adjective signalling the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra was the many-headed serpent of Greek myth killed by Heracles, a classic monster.

clue.text: Private has to respect changes

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the letters are altered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A soldier must show deference when the officers change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' reads as a soldier, but it is the adjective meaning confidential.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-secret means highly confidential, an intensified form of private.

clue.text: Intricate patterns in wing of church

indicators.note: an intricate design is elaborately interwoven, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Elaborate decoration adorns one wing of a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm of a cross-shaped church, projecting at right angles from the nave like a wing.

clue.text: Delay robbery

blocks.note: first meaning: a ... in traffic or plans
second meaning: an armed ... of a bank or coach

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated nouns that happen to share one hyphenated word.
explanation.definitionFit: A hold-up is both a stoppage that slows things down and a robbery carried out at gunpoint.

clue.text: So that the facts are clear, keep report about ambassador

definitions.text: So that the facts are clear

blocks.note: a keep is the strongest tower of a castle, a fort
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
a report is a written record

explanation.surface: A diplomat's statement is to be kept on file so the facts are plain.
explanation.walkthrough: The ambassador's title goes before the report: 'about' reads as 'on the subject of' rather than signalling a wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something for the record means stating it officially so that the facts are set down clearly.

clue.text: First-rate golfer turned back in corridor

indicators.note: turning back means facing the other way, so the golfer's name is read from right to left

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, with the digit 1 read as the letter I
Ernie Els is a South African golfer, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A top golfer turns round and heads back down a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passageway between rows of seats or shelves, a kind of corridor.

clue.text: Release one rodent into river

indicators.note: putting things into something places them inside it, so the river's name goes round them

blocks.note: taken as written
a rat is a rodent
the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: Someone sets a rodent free by dropping it into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to free someone from blame or obligation, so it can mean to release.

clue.text: I restrict others exercising a dog

indicators.note: exercising puts things through their paces and moves them about, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dog walker keeps everyone else away while walking a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish terrier, or Scottie, is a breed of dog, so the definition gives an example of the category.

clue.text: Sexton's article supporting racists, unfortunately

indicators.note: things that go unfortunately go awry, so these letters fall into a different order
in a down clue, a supporting piece sits underneath and so comes last

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A church official's newspaper piece backs bigots, regrettably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a piece of writing, but it is the grammatical word an.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristan looks after a church's sacred vessels and vestments; in a parish church the same post is a sexton.

clue.text: What may bar and tinnie, if drunk, provide?

definitions.text: What may bar and tinnie, if drunk, provide?

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters stagger into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange, ignoring 'and'

explanation.surface: A pub and a can of beer, if consumed, might supply something to make you tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: A tinnie is Australian slang for a can of beer. The whole clue is the definition and 'and' just joins the two words of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriant is an intoxicating substance, which both a bar and a can of beer supply once drunk.

clue.text: Eccentric etcher resettles in a Durham town

indicators.note: an eccentric is off-centre and odd, so the following letters are thrown into a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An oddball printmaker moves house to a town in County Durham.
explanation.walkthrough: Chester-le-Street is a market town in County Durham, north-east England, known for its county cricket ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Chester-le-Street is a real town in County Durham, so the definition names its location.

clue.text: Hairstyle in fashion? Certainly

blocks.note: the ton is an old word for high fashion
sure means certainly

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a hairstyle is in fashion and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fashion' reads as a phrase, but 'in' is only a link and 'fashion' alone gives TON.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown worn by monks, a distinctive style of cutting the hair.

clue.text: Newsworthy subject, a leader in London

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front, so only the opening letter of the city is kept

blocks.note: a subject of discussion is a topic
taken as written
the first letter of London

explanation.surface: A news item names a topic and a prominent London figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical means relating to current affairs, so a topical story is newsworthy at the moment.

clue.text: Childish supporter wearing trendy hat

indicators.note: whoever is wearing a hat has it around them, so the supporter sits inside the other pieces

blocks.note: a fan supports a team
what is trendy is in
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A football fan sports a fashionable hat and looks silly doing it.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE for a hat is dated British slang worth remembering.
explanation.definitionFit: Infantile means like an infant, so it is a synonym for childish or immature.

clue.text: Opera, big round the States

indicators.note: going round something encircles it, so the adjective wraps around the abbreviation

blocks.note: fat means big
the States is the United States, US

explanation.surface: An opera production makes a grand tour of America.
explanation.definitionFit: Faust is Gounod's opera, based on the legend of the scholar who sells his soul to the devil.

clue.text: Modest receiving second prize

indicators.note: something receiving a thing takes it in, so the abbreviation goes inside the adjective

blocks.note: modest in the sense of chaste or pure
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A humble person comes second and collects an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize' at the end looks like part of the story of winning, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A purse is a sum of money offered as a prize, especially in boxing or horse racing.

clue.text: Foe in Yemen beaten

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An adversary has been defeated in Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is an opponent or adversary, a direct synonym for foe.

clue.text: Sign for reference book he's taken out

indicators.note: what is taken out is removed, so those letters disappear from the longer word

blocks.note: a thesaurus is a reference book of synonyms
the letters to remove, taken as written

explanation.surface: A man has removed a sign that pointed to a reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus, the bull, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Secret assembly may become depressed with pound involved

indicators.note: something involved is caught up inside, so the money symbol sits within the other word

blocks.note: a depressed surface is sunken, curving inwards
L, from libra, is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: A clandestine meeting might turn gloomy once money gets involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depressed' suggests gloom but means physically hollowed.
explanation.definitionFit: A conclave is a private meeting, most famously the closed assembly of cardinals electing a pope.

clue.text: Chat with French artist, one dropping out

indicators.note: one who drops out leaves, so that letter is removed from the painter's name

blocks.note: Jean-Marc Nattier was an 18th-century French portrait painter
the Roman numeral for one is the letter to remove

explanation.surface: Someone chats with a French painter, one of a group who have quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To natter is to chatter idly at length, a British informal word for chat.

clue.text: Adulation adroitly put in a new light

indicators.note: putting something in a new light presents it differently, so the letters are shown in another order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Fawning praise has been cleverly reframed to look better.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is excessive worship or admiration, which is a strong synonym for adulation.
